summary: Roughly half the households in this 9-square-mile town earn above $250,000 a year, yet the most conspicuous local infrastructure isn't a country club—it's a network of equestrian and hiking trails threaded through the rolling western foothills of the Santa Cruz Mountains, where properties sit on large lots screened by coast live oaks and the eastern ridgelines frame unobstructed views across Silicon Valley to the Diablo Range. There is essentially no commercial district: no downtown, no traffic lights to speak of, and almost no retail or restaurant frontage within city limits, which means daily errands—groceries, coffee, dining—pull you downhill into Los Altos, Palo Alto, or Cupertino. The town functions as a residential enclave whose economy orbits the tech and research campuses clustered along the 280 corridor; Foothill College sits near the northern edge, but job centers require a car. At a median home value that exceeds $2 million against that high median income, the price-to-income ratio still lands above 8:1, and rents above $3,500 reinforce that even top-quintile earners face steep entry costs. With 9.4 hours of daily sunshine, mild year-round temperatures averaging 69°F by day, and a burglary rate notably elevated at 716 per 100K, the defining tension is textbook: extraordinary natural setting and near-total quiet, purchased at a price that includes both the mortgage and the understanding that almost everything else is somewhere else.
